title: Phnom Penh sights
sub: The main things to see, each with time from Baitong Hotel (BKK1), Nov 2026
tip: Short on time? Royal Palace and the National Museum next door in the morning, then Tuol Sleng in the afternoon. Add Choeung Ek if you have half a day (get a tuk-tuk to wait, about $15-20 return). Royal Palace: shoulders and knees covered, and it shuts at lunchtime (roughly 11am-2pm). Hours are from memory, so check before going.

places.name: Royal Palace & Silver Pagoda
notes: The big one: gold throne hall, and a pagoda floored with silver tiles
One ticket for both, about 2 hrs
Riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay) is right outside, nice at sunset

places.name: National Museum of Cambodia
notes: Best Angkor-era sculpture outside Angkor, in a red Khmer-style building
Next door to the palace, about 1 hr
Garden courtyard is a calm break from the heat

places.name: Tuol Sleng (S-21) Genocide Museum
notes: Khmer Rouge prison in a former school, heavy but essential
Get the audio guide, about 2 hrs
Closest major sight to the hotel

places.name: Choeung Ek Killing Fields
notes: Memorial stupa and mass grave site, very moving with the audio guide
Half a day with the ride, pair it with Tuol Sleng

places.name: Independence Monument
notes: Lotus-tower monument by Vann Molyvann, lit up at night
Quick photo stop, 10 min from the hotel

places.name: Wat Langka
notes: One of the oldest pagodas in the city, right by the monument
Free meditation sessions some evenings, ask at the gate

places.name: Wat Phnom
notes: The hilltop temple the city is named after
Small entry fee, 30 min, combine with Central Market
